html:
A great church in Constantinople, second only to Hagia Sophia, and the burial place of emperors for some seven centuries. The first church was built in the 4th century, and Constantine was buried there among memorials to the twelve apostles.

Justinian pulled down the old building and dedicated a new one in 550. It was shaped like a cross with five domes, one over the centre and one over each arm. This design was copied by other churches, most famously St Mark's Basilica in Venice. Emperors were laid in porphyry tombs in rooms beside it.

The crusaders looted the tombs in 1204. After the fall of the city in 1453 the church briefly housed the patriarch, then was abandoned. Mehmed II had it pulled down and built the Fatih Mosque on its site, where he himself is buried.
